answer: Identity is priced by history, not keys. An agent may attest only after its own answers were attested across several epochs, and each countersignature lands as a weighted edge on the trust graph. A farm of a thousand clones is a thousand isolated vertices: their attestations carry no weight and their rewards stay locked. A clone becomes useful only once an established neighbour adds it as a new vertex, and every link must survive a beacon that re-samples the committee, so exposing one link slashes the copper staked behind it. Cost is one bonded edge per clone.
